name: Amphetamine / Adderall

lead: Adderall is a prescription mixed-amphetamine product for ADHD and narcolepsy. Forum users discuss it for appetite control and leaning out, and some also report more social ease and gym drive.

The chain is less appetite, fewer calories, then fat loss. Appetite loss and weight loss are common documented effects, and amphetamines are listed among appetite suppressants, but no trial has tested Adderall as a weight-loss or appearance treatment in healthy people.

paras: It is prescribed as immediate- or extended-release tablets or capsules. Those who use it for appearance pair appetite control with calorie tracking and gym work. Non-medical use is common among US college students, and forum users note that unprescribed pills may not be what they claim.

Documented effects include higher heart rate and blood pressure, insomnia, anxiety, psychosis at heavy use, and dependence with withdrawal. It is Schedule II in the US, Class B in the UK and Schedule I in Canada. Unprescribed pills may contain other substances.

angle.text: Adderall suppresses appetite, so some people use it to eat less and lean out, and report more focus and gym drive. Appetite suppression is a documented effect; weight loss and looks were not what it was studied for.

lead: Adderall is a prescription mixed-salts amphetamine product containing roughly equal parts of amphetamine aspartate, amphetamine sulfate, dextroamphetamine saccharate and dextroamphetamine sulfate, used mainly for ADHD and narcolepsy [1][2]. It is a controlled substance, Schedule II in the US and Class B in the UK [2].

Loss of appetite and weight loss are common effects, and the drug is listed among appetite suppressants [2]. On looksmax.org, users discuss it for focus, appetite control, social disinhibition and gym use, and the forum also discusses obtaining it without a prescription [3][4]. No published trial has tested Adderall as a weight-loss or appearance treatment in healthy people.
Documented risks include cardiovascular effects, insomnia, anxiety, psychosis at heavy use, and addiction; surveys show non-medical use is common among US college students [5][6].
infobox: Schedule II (US); Class B (UK); Schedule I (Canada)

paras: Adderall is approved for ADHD and narcolepsy. Reviews describe long-term stimulant treatment as effective for core ADHD symptoms [2], and controlled trials of mixed amphetamine salts have been run in adults and children with ADHD [7][8]. Reference sources report that low doses can modestly improve cognition in healthy adults while higher doses impair cognitive control, and that stimulants may modestly increase strength and endurance; several sports bodies ban the drug [2].

Reduced appetite and weight loss are common adverse effects, and the FDA advises monitoring height and weight in children and adolescents because of possible reversible growth impairment [2]. Use specifically for weight loss in healthy people is off-label and not supported by dedicated trials.

Physical effects include changes in blood pressure and heart rate, dry mouth, Raynaud's phenomenon and sexual side effects; large doses can cause rhabdomyolysis and dangerous body temperature rises [2]. FDA-commissioned studies in 2011 found no link between therapeutic use and serious cardiovascular events, but use is contraindicated in existing cardiovascular disease [2]. Psychological effects include insomnia, mood swings and anxiety, with psychosis mainly at heavy use [2].

Reference sources describe a high potential for misuse. Recreational doses are far larger than therapeutic ones, tolerance develops quickly, and withdrawal is common in heavy users [2]. A national survey of 10,904 US college students examined non-medical use of prescription stimulants including Adderall, and a second survey of 4,580 students examined motives and routes of administration [5][6]. Studies have also mined Twitter for non-medical Adderall use [9].

Forum threads include users asking about first-time use for study, others describing experiences, and posts about the stimulant's effect on social inhibition, appetite and the gym [3][4]. Some users warn that pills sold without a prescription are often not Adderall; one reply to a first-time user claims such 30 mg pills are usually pressed methamphetamine, and another reply says an unprescribed purchase is likely meth [3][4]. Public health sources do not verify these specific claims, but the forum posts document the concern in the community.
No studies have tested Adderall for weight loss or appearance goals in healthy people.

ADHD trials exist: a 7-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover study of mixed amphetamine salts in 27 adults with ADHD [7], a randomized placebo-controlled study of Adderall XR in children [8], and a comparison of Ritalin and Adderall in children [10]. Registered trials have also examined mixed amphetamine salts for cocaine dependence [11][12]. A rat study reported that amphetamine reduces impulsive decision making and examined the dopaminergic and noradrenergic basis [13].
